name: Tampere University of Applied Sciences
summary: Applied-sciences university in Tampere; nine English bachelor's, from software and textile engineering to nursing, media and a run-a-company degree.

ib.text: In the January joint application TAMK selects by the International UAS Exam, SAT, or a pre-task and interview, not on IB grades. Its engineering rolling admission takes IB with English 5 and HL Maths 5.

dates.label: Rolling admission closes, 15:00, unless places fill first
International UAS Exam, online from 12:00 Finnish time
Admitted: final certificate, or proof you have graduated, due 15:00

programmes.name: Environmental Engineering and Green Transition
programmes.about: Solving environmental problems for industry and the public sector: treating waste and water, and investigating and monitoring contaminated soil, water and air, with field and lab work.
programmes.overview: The programme prepares international engineers for the energy and environmental industries, with a practical focus on waste and water treatment and on investigating and monitoring contaminated soil, water and air. Study topics include ecosystems, soil and groundwater, water and sanitation, ecotoxicology and waste management, so that industrial and public production processes can be run sustainably. You learn to carry out sampling and analysis in the field and in the laboratory, in an international community, and degrees of this kind usually include a practical training period and a final thesis. Graduates usually work with process, water, waste and environmental monitoring tasks in industry, utilities and consultancies.
programmes.ib: Rolling admission on IB grades (English 5, HL Maths 5) plus interview; in January, the UAS Exam or SAT.
programmes.selectionNote: January: UAS Exam (10 places) or SAT (5). Rolling, 15 Nov–28 Feb: IB grades or SAT, then an interview (rounds in Dec, Jan, Feb), until places fill.

programmes.name: Software Engineering
programmes.about: Software engineering for the international ICT industry, covering AI, cloud computing and cyber security, with sustainability and ethics throughout and project-based learning.
programmes.overview: The curriculum moves from programming fundamentals to web and mobile development, user interfaces, usability and software regulation, and on to artificial intelligence, data-driven systems, cloud computing and cybersecurity, with sustainability, ethics and responsible technology use woven in. The programme combines technical skills with collaboration, problem-solving and communication, and prepares you to work in international and multidisciplinary environments. Graduates can work as software engineers, developers, architects, consultants, data or AI engineers, web or mobile application developers and cloud solution specialists.
programmes.ib: Rolling admission on IB grades (English 5, HL Maths 5) plus interview; in January, the UAS Exam or SAT.
programmes.selectionNote: January: UAS Exam (35 places) or SAT (5). Rolling, 15 Nov–28 Feb: IB grades or SAT, then an interview (rounds in Dec, Jan, Feb), until places fill.

programmes.name: Textile and Material Engineering
programmes.about: Sustainable textile engineering: materials, manufacturing and industry practice, learned through projects, lab exercises and work with companies, with options to study or train abroad.
programmes.overview: You study textile materials and manufacturing processes from fibres to finished products, with textile recycling, the circular economy, industrial economics, quality management, supply chain and project management, on a base of mathematics, chemistry and physics. Electives span business, entrepreneurship and environmental engineering. Teaching combines contact teaching, online learning, project work, laboratory exercises and industry collaboration, with mandatory practical training and exchange or overseas internships available. Everything is taught in English, with attention to the changing textile and fashion sector. Graduates work in production, product development, quality assurance and supply chains.
programmes.ib: Rolling admission on IB grades (English 5, HL Maths 5) plus interview; in January, the UAS Exam or SAT.
programmes.selectionNote: January: UAS Exam (8 places) or SAT (2). Rolling, 15 Nov–28 Feb: IB grades or SAT, then an interview (rounds in Dec, Jan, Feb), until places fill.

programmes.name: International Business
programmes.about: Practice-based international business with a required study period abroad and eight specialisation options, including accounting, digital business and sustainable entrepreneurship.
programmes.overview: You learn core business theory and apply it, choosing two specialisation modules from eight options: Accounting and Finance, Digital Business, Experience Economy, Human Resource Management and Leadership, Innovation Management and Business Development, Digital Marketing, Supply Chain Management, and Sustainable Entrepreneurship. First-year students run a Virtual Firm, and later work comes through case studies, company projects and team assignments, led by coaches, with a study period abroad as a required part of the degree. Double-degree partners are in Belgium, France and Germany. Graduates work in marketing, sales, supply chain management, project management, consulting and entrepreneurship in Finland and abroad.
programmes.selectionNote: All 40 places go on the International UAS Exam (23 Mar 2027); IB grades do not count.

programmes.name: Business in Finland
programmes.about: A broad business degree with Finland-specific professional studies and Finnish built in, so you gain the skills to stay, work and build a career in Finland after graduating.
programmes.overview: The programme joins a broad business foundation with studies specific to Finland: Finnish corporate culture, business practice and legislation, with compulsory Finnish language learning built into the coursework rather than set apart. The first year introduces business in Finland, the second deepens competence through applied projects, the third offers professional exposure and the fourth ends with a bachelor's thesis, with elective professional studies and free-choice courses along the way. It is aimed at international students who want to build a career in Finland, and it addresses gaps employers have identified in graduates' knowledge of Finnish workplace culture.
programmes.ib: International UAS Exam. Finnish language learning is built into the degree.
programmes.selectionNote: All 40 places go on the International UAS Exam (23 Mar 2027); IB grades do not count.

programmes.name: Team Entrepreneurship
programmes.about: Learning entrepreneurship by running real businesses with classmates at TAMK Proakatemia, through team learning and coaching rather than lectures, in an international community.
programmes.overview: You study leadership and management, sales and marketing, financial management, teamwork, and the creation of new services, products and business models, and develop skills such as collaboration, communication, emotional intelligence and critical thinking. Rather than classes in the usual sense, you learn through teamwork, dialogue and weekly reflection guided by professional team coaches, running real businesses as a co-founder, working with actual clients and building projects that earn revenue. The pedagogy has over 25 years of history in entrepreneurship education, and the programme forms an entrepreneurial community of alumni, coaches and business partners. It prepares you for a path as a founder or leader.
programmes.ib: Pre-task assignment with your application, then an online interview.
programmes.selectionNote: Pre-task due with the application (21 Jan 2027, 15:00); the top 160 get an online group interview on 9–11 Feb 2027. IB grades do not count.

programmes.name: Media and Arts
programmes.about: Practical skills for the international culture sector with new media tools, on one of three paths: Fine Art Lab, Interactive Media, or Music and Event Production.
programmes.overview: In the first year you pick one of three tracks, Interactive Media, Music and Event Production, or Fine Art Lab, with further modules in game design, sound design and fine art photography. You build a personal curriculum from the study modules, combining your specialisation with electives, and learn to develop ideas into finished products that succeed artistically, technically and economically. Practical training and exchange studies abroad are part of the offer. The programme is based at Mediapolis, a media campus that houses companies including the broadcaster YLE. Graduates work as experts, developers and entrepreneurs in games, music and live events, new media, service design and art galleries.
programmes.ib: Pre-task assignment (published 26 November 2026) and an online interview; no English certificate needed.
programmes.selectionNote: Choose one path (Fine Art Lab 24, Interactive Media 33, Music 23 places). Pre-task (out 26 Nov) due 21 Jan 2027; online interview 9–11 Mar. IB grades do not count.

programmes.name: Early Childhood Education and Care
programmes.about: Early childhood education, social pedagogy and social services for non-native Finnish speakers, taught bilingually, qualifying you as an ECEC social pedagogue in Finland.
programmes.overview: You combine theory and practical skills in social services, early childhood education and social pedagogy, with special attention to intercultural communication and language development, and Finnish as a second language studies built into the degree. The programme is bilingual: it starts mainly in English and shifts toward Finnish as it advances, and it is designed for students whose first language is not Finnish. It meets the requirements of Finland's early childhood education law, so you qualify as an early childhood education social pedagogue. Graduates can work in early childhood education, child protection, schools, youth work, private companies and non-profit organisations.
programmes.ib: International UAS Exam; English at B2. Aimed at non-native Finnish speakers.
programmes.selectionNote: All 20 places go on the International UAS Exam (23 Mar 2027); IB grades do not count.

programmes.name: Bilingual Degree Programme in Nursing
programmes.about: Training for Finland's regulated nursing profession, from basic skills to independent practice, with clinical placements and Finnish learned alongside nursing.
programmes.overview: You study foundational nursing and move to advanced clinical care, from patient safety, ethical and client-centred care and everyday nursing work to clinical reasoning and evidence-based decision-making, with Finnish language study built into the professional courses. The programme is functionally bilingual, starting mainly in English and bringing in more Finnish as it advances, and it includes extensive supervised clinical placements in real healthcare environments. It serves people who do not yet speak Finnish and leads to an EU-recognised qualification as a registered nurse. Graduates work in primary and specialised health care and the private sector, in hospitals, health centres, companies and non-profit organisations.
programmes.ib: International UAS Exam; English at B2. Taught in English and Finnish.
programmes.selectionNote: All 66 places go on the International UAS Exam (23 Mar 2027); IB grades do not count.

notes: Your IB grades count only in the engineering rolling admission; everywhere else you are chosen by an exam, SAT or pre-task.
Nursing, Early Childhood Education and Business in Finland build Finnish into the degree and are aimed at people who want to work in Finland.
Team Entrepreneurship (Proakatemia) replaces lectures with running a real company with your classmates.
